name: India
summary: The Republic of India — a sovereign subcontinent stretching from the Himalayas to the Indian Ocean.

profile.Flag: Tricolour of saffron, white, and green with 24-spoke navy Ashoka Chakra in centre
profile.Food: Khichdi, Biryani, Roti, Dal, Dosa
profile.Sweets: Gulab Jamun, Jalebi, Laddu, Kheer
profile.Crafts: Zari embroidery, Handloom textiles, Brassware, Blue pottery

points: Ancient cradle of the Indus Valley Civilisation flourishing c. 2500 BCE
Unified under Mauryan Empire under Ashoka the Great in 3rd century BCE
Gained independence from British rule on 15 August 1947
Adopted the Constitution of India on 26 January 1950 establishing a sovereign democratic republic
source: Census of India 2011, Government of India, Wikipedia

name: Andhra Pradesh
summary: The Sunrise State on the southeastern coast, cradle of Telugu culture and Kuchipudi dance.

profile.Flag: Emblem depicts Purna Ghatam (vase of plenty) flanked by lotus buds and Ashoka lions
profile.Food: Pesarattu, Gongura Pachadi, Royyala Iguru, Ulava Charu
profile.Sweets: Pootharekulu, Kakinada Kaja, Bobbatlu
profile.Crafts: Kalamkari block prints, Kondapalli wooden toys, Dharmavaram silk, Etikoppaka lacquer toys

points: Ruled by the Satavahana dynasty from 2nd century BCE to 2nd century CE with capital at Amaravati
Flourished under Eastern Chalukyas (7th–11th century) and Kakatiya dynasty (12th–14th century)
Formed on 1 October 1953 as the first linguistic state in independent India
Bifurcated in June 2014 creating the separate state of Telangana
source: Census of India 2011, Andhra Pradesh Govt, ODOP, Wikipedia

name: Arunachal Pradesh
summary: The Land of the Dawn-Lit Mountains in India's eastern Himalayas, famed for Tawang Monastery and tribal biodiversity.

profile.Flag: Emblem depicts the sun rising behind twin Himalayan peaks over Mithun head and Ashoka lions
profile.Food: Thukpa, Zan, Bamboo Shoot Pork Fry, Lukter
profile.Sweets: Khapse (Tibetan deep-fried pastry)
profile.Crafts: Monpa handmade paper, Sherdukpen wooden masks, Wancho woodcarvings, Apatani handloom

points: Historical home to 26 major indigenous tribes with distinct customs and languages
Tawang Monastery founded in 1680-1681 by Merak Lama Lodre Gyatso
Administered as North-East Frontier Agency (NEFA) until designated Union Territory in 1972
Attained full statehood on 20 February 1987 as India's 24th state
source: Census of India 2011, Government of Arunachal Pradesh, ODOP, Wikipedia

name: Assam
summary: Gateway to Northeast India, known for Assam CTC tea, Golden Muga silk, and Kaziranga rhinos along the Brahmaputra.

profile.Flag: Emblem features Kaziranga one-horned rhino against green mountains and the Brahmaputra River
profile.Food: Khaar, Masor Tenga (sour fish curry), Duck with Ash Gourd, Pitika
profile.Sweets: Pitha, Laru (sesame & coconut balls), Jolpan
profile.Crafts: Muga golden silk sarees, Jaapi conical cane hats, Bell metal craft of Sarthebari, Terracotta of Asharikandi

points: Known anciently as Pragjyotisha and Kamarupa kingdoms, mentioned in the Mahabharata
Ahom kingdom ruled for nearly 600 years (1228–1826) successfully resisting Mughal invasions
Battle of Saraighat in 1671 led by General Lachit Borphukan defeated the Mughal forces
Became a British province following the Treaty of Yandabo in 1826
source: Census of India 2011, Government of Assam, ODOP, Wikipedia

name: Bihar
summary: Historical cradle of Magadha, Nalanda University, Buddhism at Bodh Gaya, and Jainism in Rajgir.

profile.Flag: Emblem features the sacred Bodhi Tree between two swastika symbols enclosed by bricks
profile.Food: Litti Chokha, Sattu Paratha, Dal Pitha, Chana Ghugni
profile.Sweets: Thekua, Khaja of Silao, Tilkut of Gaya, Anarsa
profile.Crafts: Madhubani (Mithila) paintings, Sikki grass crafts, Bhagalpuri Tussar silk, Sujani embroidery

points: Center of ancient empires: Haryanka, Nanda, Mauryan, and Gupta dynasties based at Pataliputra
Gautama Buddha attained Enlightenment under the Bodhi Tree in Bodh Gaya around 5th century BCE
Nalanda University established in the 5th century CE flourished as a global seat of learning
Separated from Bengal Presidency in 1912 and attained present state boundaries with Jharkhand separation in 2000
source: Census of India 2011, Government of Bihar, ODOP, Wikipedia

name: Chhattisgarh
summary: Mineral-rich heartland endowed with sal forests, Chitrakote Falls, and Dhokra lost-wax bronze crafts.

profile.Flag: Emblem has 36 outer ramparts representing 36 ancient forts surrounding Ashoka lions and grain ears
profile.Food: Chila, Fara, Muthia, Bafauri, Dubki Kadi
profile.Sweets: Dehrori, Kusli, Gulgule
profile.Crafts: Bastar Dhokra bell metal casting, Wrought iron craft, Kosa silk sarees, Terracotta pottery

points: Known anciently as Dakshina Kosala with mention in the Ramayana
Ruled by Kalachuris of Ratanpur from 10th to 18th century CE who established 36 garhs (forts)
Maratha Bhonsle dynasty ruled until British takeover in 1854
Carved out of southeastern Madhya Pradesh on 1 November 2000 as a separate state
source: Census of India 2011, Government of Chhattisgarh, ODOP, Wikipedia

name: Goa
summary: Konkan coastal paradise famed for golden sands, Portuguese UNESCO churches, spice plantations, and seafood.

profile.Flag: Emblem depicts a Vriksha Deep (traditional brass lamp) surrounded by coconut palms
profile.Food: Goan Fish Curry Rice, Pork Vindaloo, Xacuti, Sorpotel
profile.Sweets: Bebinca, Dodol, Serradura, Bolinhas
profile.Crafts: Kunbi handloom sarees, Azulejos hand-painted ceramic tiles, Coconut shell carving, Brassware

points: Ruled by Kadambas of Goa (10th–14th century) and Bahmani Sultanate before Bijapur Sultanate
Conquered by Portuguese explorer Afonso de Albuquerque in 1510, lasting 451 years as Portuguese India
Liberated by the Indian Armed Forces during Operation Vijay on 19 December 1961
Conferred full statehood on 30 May 1987 as India's 25th state
source: Census of India 2011, Government of Goa, ODOP, Wikipedia

name: Gujarat
summary: Land of Mahatma Gandhi, Gir Asiatic lions, Rann of Kutch white salt desert, and the Statue of Unity.

profile.Flag: Emblem features Ashoka lions encircled by sacred bull and horse motifs from Indus Valley seals
profile.Food: Dhokla, Khandvi, Thepla, Undhiyu, Sev Khamani
profile.Sweets: Mohanthal, Basundi, Shrikhand, Sukhdi, Ghari
profile.Crafts: Patan Patola double-ikat silk, Bandhani tie-dye, Kutch Rogan art, Sankheda lacquered wood

points: Home to major Harappan port city Lothal with world's earliest known dry dock (c. 2400 BCE)
Ruled by Chaulukya (Solanki) dynasty (10th–13th century) who constructed Rani ki Vav and Sun Temple Modhera
Birthplace of Mahatma Gandhi (Porbandar, 1869) and Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel (Nadiad, 1875)
Bifurcated from Bombay State on 1 May 1960 on linguistic lines
source: Census of India 2011, Government of Gujarat, ODOP, Wikipedia

name: Haryana
summary: Agricultural giant and industrial cyber hub surrounding New Delhi, site of legendary Kurukshetra.

profile.Flag: Emblem depicts a radiant rising sun over lotus blossoms and water streams with wheat ears
profile.Food: Bajra Khichdi, Kadhi Pakora, Kachri ki Sabzi, Besan Masala Roti
profile.Sweets: Gond ke Laddu, Churma, Pinni, Malpua
profile.Crafts: Panipat handloom carpets and durries, Rewari brass sheets, Rohtak pottery, Tilla juttis

points: Site of the epic Kurukshetra War described in the Mahabharata and birthplace of the Bhagavad Gita
Three historic Battles of Panipat (1526, 1556, 1761) shaped medieval and modern Indian history
Part of Punjab Province under British rule until independence in 1947
Formed on 1 November 1966 on linguistic recommendation of the Shah Commission
source: Census of India 2011, Government of Haryana, ODOP, Wikipedia

name: Himachal Pradesh
summary: Devbhoomi in the Western Himalayas known for apple orchards, snow-capped ranges, and hill stations.

profile.Flag: Emblem features three snow-peaked Himalayan mountain summits over the river streams
profile.Food: Himachali Dham, Siddu, Madra, Chha Gosht, Babru
profile.Sweets: Mittha (sweetened saffron rice), Bhey, Patande
profile.Crafts: Kullu and Kinnauri shawls, Chamba Rumal embroidered handkerchiefs, Kangra miniature paintings, Chamba chappals

points: Historic kingdom of Trigarta mentioned in the Mahabharata ruled the Kangra Valley
Shimla declared the Summer Capital of British India in 1864
Integrated 30 princely states into Himachal Pradesh as Chief Commissioner's province in 1948
Attained full statehood on 25 January 1971 as India's 18th state
source: Census of India 2011, Government of Himachal Pradesh, ODOP, Wikipedia

name: Jharkhand
summary: The Land of Forests endowed with 40% of India's minerals, sacred Parasnath hill, and waterfalls.

profile.Flag: Emblem features seven concentric circles with Ashoka lions, Palash flowers, and green rings
profile.Food: Dhuska, Rugra mushroom curry, Pittha, Chilka Roti, Bamboo Shoot curry
profile.Sweets: Arsa Roti, Tilkut, Dudhori
profile.Crafts: Sohrai and Khovar wall mural art, Dhokra brass figurines, Terracotta tiles, Bamboo baskets

points: Tribal Chota Nagpur kingdoms governed by Munda, Santhal, and Oraon communities for millennia
Birsa Munda led the Ulgulan rebellion (1899–1900) against British colonial land policies
Jamshedpur founded by Jamsetji Tata in 1907 as India's first planned industrial steel city
Created as an independent state from southern Bihar on 15 November 2000
source: Census of India 2011, Government of Jharkhand, ODOP, Wikipedia

name: Karnataka
summary: Land of Vijayanagara ruins at Hampi, Mysore Palace, Hoysala temples, coffee plantations, and Silicon Valley Bengaluru.

profile.Flag: Emblem features the Gandaberunda (mythical two-headed eagle) flanked by twin red lions
profile.Food: Bisi Bele Bath, Mysore Masala Dosa, Akki Rotti, Ragi Mudde, Jolada Rotti, Kundapura Chicken
profile.Sweets: Mysore Pak, Dharwad Peda, Belagavi Kunda, Gokak Karadantu, Holige
profile.Crafts: Mysore Sandalwood carving, Channapatna lacquer toys, Ilkal & Mysore silk sarees, Bidriware metalwork

points: Ruled by Kadamba, Western Chalukya, Rashtrakuta, Hoysala, and Vijayanagara empires
Vijayanagara Empire (1336–1565) built majestic capital at Hampi, UNESCO World Heritage site
Kingdom of Mysore under the Wadiyar dynasty transformed modern state infrastructure
Formed as Mysore State on 1 November 1956 and renamed Karnataka on 1 November 1973
source: Census of India 2011, Government of Karnataka, ODOP, Wikipedia

name: Kerala
summary: God's Own Country on the Malabar Coast, famed for backwaters, Kathakali dance, Ayurvedic traditions, and spices.

profile.Flag: Emblem depicts two elephants guarding the imperial conch shell of Travancore encircled by coconut fronds
profile.Food: Appam with Ishtu, Kerala Sadya on banana leaf, Malabar Parotta with Beef Roast, Karimeen Pollichathu
profile.Sweets: Ada Pradhaman, Unniyappam, Palada Payasam, Kozhikode Halwa
profile.Crafts: Aranmula metal mirrors, Kasavu gold-bordered handlooms, Bell metal craft of Mannar, Coir floor mats

points: Muziris port carried global spice trade with ancient Greeks, Romans, and Arabs from 1st millennium BCE
Chera dynasty (3rd century BCE–12th century CE) ruled from Mahodayapuram (Kodungallur)
Battle of Colachel in 1741: King Marthanda Varma of Travancore defeated the Dutch East India Company
State of Kerala formed on 1 November 1956 merging Travancore, Cochin, and Malabar regions
source: Census of India 2011, Government of Kerala, ODOP, Wikipedia

name: Madhya Pradesh
summary: Heart of India, Tiger State boasting Khajuraho temples, Sanchi Stupa, Gwalior Fort, and Kanha tiger reserve.

profile.Flag: Emblem features a lion capital inside a banyan tree encircled by 24 stupas and wheat stalks
profile.Food: Poha Jalebi, Bhutte Ka Kees, Dal Bafla, Rogan Josh, Biryani of Bhopal
profile.Sweets: Mawa Bati, Malpua of Hoshangabad, Khurma, Kopra Pak
profile.Crafts: Chanderi silk-cotton sarees, Maheshwari woven sarees, Bagh block printing, Bell metal craft

points: Emperor Ashoka erected the Great Stupa at Sanchi in the 3rd century BCE
Chandela dynasty constructed the magnificent erotic and spiritual temples of Khajuraho (950–1050 CE)
Raja Bhoj of Paramara dynasty ruled from Dhar and constructed Bhojpur temple in 11th century
Formed on 1 November 1956 and reorganized in 2000 with the separation of Chhattisgarh
source: Census of India 2011, Government of Madhya Pradesh, ODOP, Wikipedia

name: Maharashtra
summary: Economic powerhouse of India, financial capital Mumbai, Maratha hill forts of Chhatrapati Shivaji, and Ajanta-Ellora caves.

profile.Flag: Emblem features the circular seal of Shivaji Maharaj inscribed in Sanskrit surrounded by 16 lotus buds
profile.Food: Vada Pav, Pav Bhaji, Misal Pav, Puran Poli, Kanda Poha, Solkadhi, Kolhapuri Tambda Rassa
profile.Sweets: Modak, Shrikhand, Puran Poli, Basundi, Kaju Katli
profile.Crafts: Paithani silk sarees, Kolhapuri leather chappals, Warli tribal folk paintings, Himroo shawls

points: Satavahana dynasty (2nd century BCE–2nd century CE) carved early rock-cut monuments at Karla and Ajanta
Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj founded the Maratha Empire in 1674 pioneering guerrilla naval warfare
Peshwas expanded the Maratha confederacy across northern and central India in the 18th century
State of Maharashtra created on 1 May 1960 following the Samyukta Maharashtra movement
source: Census of India 2011, Government of Maharashtra, ODOP, Wikipedia

name: Manipur
summary: Jewel of India, celebrated for classical Manipuri Raas Leela dance, floating phumdis of Loktak Lake, and martial arts.

profile.Flag: Emblem features the mythical dragon creature Kanglasha guarding the historical Kangla Palace
profile.Food: Kangshoi vegetable stew, Eromba fish mash, Singju spicy salad, Chak-hao black rice kheer
profile.Sweets: Kabok (puffed rice snacks), Chak-hao Kheer
profile.Crafts: Longpi black stone pottery, Kauna water reed mats, Shaphee Lanphee embroidered shawls, Bamboo baskets

points: Ningthouja dynasty ruled Kangleipak (ancient Manipur) from Kangla Fort beginning in 33 CE
Birthplace of modern Polo (Sagol Kangjei), codified by the British from traditional Manipuri games
Battle of Imphal in 1944 turned the tide of World War II against Japanese advance into India
Merged with the Union of India in 1949 and attained full statehood on 21 January 1972
source: Census of India 2011, Government of Manipur, ODOP, Wikipedia

name: Meghalaya
summary: Abode of Clouds in the Khasi and Garo hills, famous for bio-engineered living root bridges and Cherrapunji rains.

profile.Flag: Emblem depicts three mountain ranges with rain clouds and traditional Khasi ceremonial shield
profile.Food: Jadoh (rice cooked with meat), Doh-neiiong (pork with black sesame), Tungrymbai, Pumaloi
profile.Sweets: Pukhlein (sweet jaggery rice fritter), Sakin Gata
profile.Crafts: Cane and bamboo stools, Ryndia Eri silk handloom shawls, Wood carving of Garo hills

points: Traditional matrilineal social structure where lineage and inheritance trace through the mother
Bio-engineered living root bridges constructed by Khasi tribes from Ficus elastica aerial roots
Mawsynram and Sohra (Cherrapunji) record the highest average annual rainfall on Earth (>11,000 mm)
Carved out of Assam as an autonomous region in 1970 and granted full statehood on 21 January 1972
source: Census of India 2011, Government of Meghalaya, ODOP, Wikipedia

name: Mizoram
summary: Land of the Rolling Hills and high bamboo ridges, celebrated for Cheraw bamboo dance and hospitable community culture.

profile.Flag: Emblem features a traditional Mizo drum (Khuang) between paddy sheaves over Blue Mountain
profile.Food: Bai (steamed vegetables with fermented pork), Vawksa Rep, Sawhchiar rice porridge
profile.Sweets: Koat Pitha (deep-fried banana and rice flour cakes)
profile.Crafts: Puan traditional handloom wraps, Bamboo hat (Khumbeu), Cane furniture and woven baskets

points: Ancestral Mizo clans migrated across Chin Hills into present territory in 16th to 18th century
Lushai Hills District annexed by the British Empire in 1895
Mizo Peace Accord signed in 1986 bringing peaceful end to two decades of insurgency
Granted full statehood on 20 February 1987 as the 23rd state of India with over 91% literacy
source: Census of India 2011, Government of Mizoram, ODOP, Wikipedia

name: Nagaland
summary: Land of Festivals and warrior traditions, home to 16 major Naga tribes and the international Hornbill Festival.

profile.Flag: Emblem depicts a majestic Mithun standing on green hill flanked by crossed Naga spears and shield
profile.Food: Smoked Pork with Axone (fermented soya), Bamboo Steamed Fish, Raja Mircha (Bhut Jolokia) chutney
profile.Sweets: Napnang (sweet sticky black rice pudding)
profile.Crafts: Naga warrior shawls (Tsungkotepsu), Wood carved ceremonial drinking cups, Bead jewelry, Cane baskets

points: Home to 16 major distinct Naga tribes with ancient self-governing village republics
World War II Battle of Kohima (April–June 1944) stopped the Japanese 15th Army invasion of India
Inaugurated as the 16th state of the Indian Union on 1 December 1963
Host to the annual Hornbill Festival celebrated every December at Kisama heritage village
source: Census of India 2011, Government of Nagaland, ODOP, Wikipedia

name: Odisha
summary: Soul of Incredible India, celebrated for Jagannath Puri Ratha Yatra, Konark Sun Temple, and Chilika lagoon.

profile.Flag: Emblem depicts the warrior horse statue of Konark Sun Temple flanking Ashoka lion capital
profile.Food: Dalma, Pakhala Bhata, Santula, Machha Besara, Crab Kalia
profile.Sweets: Chhena Poda (baked cheese cake), Rasagola of Pahala, Chhena Gaja, Rasabali
profile.Crafts: Pattachitra scroll paintings, Silver Filigree (Tarakasi) of Cuttack, Sambalpuri Ikat textiles, Pipili applique

points: Kalinga War (261 BCE) fought here prompted Emperor Ashoka to renounce violence and embrace Buddhism
Eastern Ganga dynasty ruled (11th–15th century) building the Jagannath Temple Puri and Konark Sun Temple
Gajapati Empire under Kapilendra Deva extended from the Ganges to the Kaveri in the 15th century
Formed on 1 April 1936 as the first province created on linguistic basis in British India (celebrated as Utkala Dibasa)
source: Census of India 2011, Government of Odisha, ODOP, Wikipedia

name: Punjab
summary: Land of Five Rivers, spiritual home of Sikhism with the Golden Temple, lively Bhangra, and granary of India.

profile.Flag: Emblem features Ashoka lions over encircled wheat stalks and twin swords
profile.Food: Makki di Roti with Sarson da Saag, Butter Chicken, Dal Makhani, Amritsari Kulcha, Chole Bhature
profile.Sweets: Pinni, Gajrela (carrot halwa), Kada Prasad, Jalebi
profile.Crafts: Phulkari floral embroidery, Amritsari juttis, Durries of Mansa, Wooden furniture of Kartarpur

points: Rigveda composed largely in ancient Punjab region along Saraswati and Indus river basins
Guru Nanak Dev founded Sikhism in 15th century; Golden Temple built by Guru Arjan in 16th century
Maharaja Ranjit Singh founded sovereign Sikh Empire (1799–1849) uniting northwest subcontinent
Divided during 1947 partition; modern Indian Punjab reorganized on linguistic lines on 1 November 1966
source: Census of India 2011, Government of Punjab, ODOP, Wikipedia

name: Rajasthan
summary: Land of Kings, famed for desert hilltop forts, marble palaces, Thar desert dunes, and colorful Rajput history.

profile.Flag: Emblem features a golden chariot wheel with Ashoka lions and the state motto
profile.Food: Dal Baati Churma, Gatte ki Sabzi, Ker Sangri, Laal Maas, Pyaaz Kachori
profile.Sweets: Ghevar, Mawa Kachori of Jodhpur, Malpua of Pushkar, Sohan Halwa
profile.Crafts: Blue Pottery of Jaipur, Sanganeri block prints, Thewa gold-glass jewelry, Bikaner camel leather craft

points: Largest Indian state by land area, home to medieval Rajput clans: Sisodias, Rathores, and Kachhwahas
Maharana Pratap of Mewar resisted Mughal expansion at the Battle of Haldighati in 1576
Six Hill Forts of Rajasthan inscribed as UNESCO World Heritage Sites (Amer, Kumbhalgarh, Chittorgarh, etc.)
Formed in stages from 22 princely states between 1948 and 1956 into the unified state of Rajasthan
source: Census of India 2011, Government of Rajasthan, ODOP, Wikipedia

name: Sikkim
summary: Himalayan jewel crowned by Mount Kangchenjunga, Rumtek monastery, alpine rhododendrons, and 100% organic farms.

profile.Flag: Emblem features the Khorlo (Buddhist prayer wheel) encircled by lotus petals and twin dragons
profile.Food: Momos, Thukpa, Gundruk fermented soup, Phagshapa pork curry, Sel Roti
profile.Sweets: Saelroti, Chhurpi dried cheese dessert
profile.Crafts: Thangka religious scroll paintings, Choktse foldable wooden tables, Lepcha handloom weaves, Woollen carpets

points: Namgyal Chogyal dynasty founded Buddhist monarchy in 1642 at Yuksom
Khangchendzonga National Park inscribed as India's first and only mixed UNESCO World Heritage Site
Became an Indian protectorate in 1950 following treaty between Chogyal and New Delhi
Joined the Indian Union as its 22nd state on 16 May 1975 following a statewide referendum
source: Census of India 2011, Government of Sikkim, ODOP, Wikipedia

name: Tamil Nadu
summary: Cradle of classical Dravidian temple architecture, Bharatanatyam dance, Carnatic music, and ancient maritime empires.

profile.Flag: Emblem depicts the 11-tiered Western gopuram of Srivilliputhur Andal Temple with Ashoka lions
profile.Food: Idli with Sambhar, Masala Dosa, Chettinad Chicken, Pongal, Filter Coffee, Rasam, Kuzhambu
profile.Sweets: Tirunelveli Halwa, Kovilpatti Kadalai Mittai, Mysore Pak, Palani Panchamirtham
profile.Crafts: Kanchipuram silk sarees, Tanjore gold foil paintings, Thanjavur art plates, Swamimalai bronze idols

points: Sangam literature period (c. 300 BCE–300 CE) represents one of the oldest classical poetic corpora on earth
Chola Empire under Rajaraja I and Rajendra I (10th–11th century) projected naval power across Southeast Asia
Constructed monumental stone gopurams at Thanjavur, Madurai, Srirangam, and Gangaikonda Cholapuram
Madras State renamed Tamil Nadu in January 1969 under Chief Minister C. N. Annadurai
source: Census of India 2011, Government of Tamil Nadu, ODOP, Wikipedia

name: Telangana
summary: Dynamic technology powerhouse and historic Deccan crossroad, home to Charminar, Kakatiya temples, and Golconda Fort.

profile.Flag: Emblem features the Kakatiya Kala Thoranam arch over the minarets of Charminar and Ashoka lions
profile.Food: Hyderabadi Dum Biryani, Haleem, Mirchi ka Salan, Sakinalu, Sarva Pindi
profile.Sweets: Qubani ka Meetha, Double ka Meetha, Ariselu, Sunnundalu
profile.Crafts: Pochampally Ikat silk, Gadwal sarees, Bidriware silver inlay, Cheriyal scroll paintings, Pembarthi metal crafts

points: Kakatiya dynasty (1158–1323) built Ramappa Temple (UNESCO site), Warangal Fort, and extensive irrigation tanks
Qutb Shahi dynasty established Golconda Sultanate and built the Charminar in 1591
Nizam of Hyderabad ruled the largest princely state until accession to Indian Union in September 1948 (Operation Polo)
Emerged as India's 29th state on 2 June 2014 following decades of civil statehood movement
source: Census of India 2011, Government of Telangana, ODOP, Wikipedia

name: Tripura
summary: Northeast state featuring Ujjayanta Palace, Neermahal lake palace, rock-cut Shiva carvings of Unakoti, and bamboo art.

profile.Flag: Emblem features the royal Manikya trident (Trishula) flanked by sacred bamboo stalks
profile.Food: Mui Borok (fermented fish Berma dishes), Kosoi Bwtwi, Mosdeng Serma, Wahan Mosdeng
profile.Sweets: Awan Bangwi (sticky rice cakes wrapped in Lairu leaf), Chhanar Payesh
profile.Crafts: Tripura bamboo and cane table mats, Hand-woven Risa and Rikutu ethnic textiles, Wood carvings

points: Manikya dynasty ruled the independent princely state of Twipra uninterrupted for centuries
Colossal 8th–9th century rock-cut Shiva reliefs carved into the hill faces of Unakoti
Maharaja Bir Bikram Kishore Manikya constructed the iconic Neermahal water palace in 1930
Acceded to India in October 1949 and attained full statehood on 21 January 1972
source: Census of India 2011, Government of Tripura, ODOP, Wikipedia

name: Uttar Pradesh
summary: Most populous state in India, heart of Gangetic civilization, home to Taj Mahal, Varanasi ghats, Ayodhya, and Lucknow.

profile.Flag: Emblem features the confluence of holy rivers Ganga and Yamuna with Matsya (twin fish) and bow of Rama
profile.Food: Awadhi Biryani, Tunday Kebabs, Bedai Aloo, Banarasi Tamatar Chaat, Nihari, Baati Chokha
profile.Sweets: Agra Petha, Mathura Peda, Banarasi Malaiyo, Imarti, Makhan Malai
profile.Crafts: Banarasi silk brocades, Chikankari white-work embroidery of Lucknow, Brassware of Moradabad, Bhadohi hand-knotted carpets, Kannauj attar perfumes

points: Core of ancient Vedic civilization; setting of Ramayana (Ayodhya) and Mahabharata (Hastinapur, Mathura)
Varanasi revered as one of the world's oldest continuously inhabited sacred cities along the Ganges
Mughal imperial capital at Agra (1526–1648) witnessed construction of Taj Mahal and Fatehpur Sikri
Renamed Uttar Pradesh on 24 January 1950 from the colonial United Provinces
source: Census of India 2011, Government of Uttar Pradesh, ODOP, Wikipedia

name: Uttarakhand
summary: Devbhoomi in the Central Himalayas, origin of holy Ganga and Yamuna, Char Dham pilgrimage, and Nanda Devi peak.

profile.Flag: Emblem depicts four mountain ridges with three water waves of Ganga and Ashoka lions
profile.Food: Kafuli, Chainssoo, Phaanu, Aloo ke Gutke, Bhatt ki Churkani
profile.Sweets: Bal Mithai of Almora, Singodi, Jhangore ki Kheer, Arsa
profile.Crafts: Aipan ritual floor art of Kumaon, Ringal bamboo basketry, Woodcarvings of Garhwal, Woollen Pankhi blankets

points: Sacred setting of the holy Char Dham: Badrinath, Kedarnath, Gangotri, and Yamunotri
Katyuri dynasty (7th–11th century) united Garhwal and Kumaon valleys with capital at Baijnath
Birthplace of the peaceful Chipko environmental conservation movement in 1973 in Chamoli
Carved out of northwestern Uttar Pradesh on 9 November 2000 as Uttaranchal, renamed Uttarakhand in 2007
source: Census of India 2011, Government of Uttarakhand, ODOP, Wikipedia

name: West Bengal
summary: Cultural and intellectual heartland of modern India, home to Nobel laureates, Durga Puja, Darjeeling tea, and Sundarbans tigers.

profile.Flag: Emblem features the globe with the Bengali letter 'Ba' inside green leaves
profile.Food: Shorshe Ilish (hilsa in mustard), Kosha Mangsho, Chingri Malai Curry, Shukto, Luchi with Cholar Dal
profile.Sweets: Rosogolla, Mishti Doi, Sandesh, Cham Cham, Pantua, Ledikeni
profile.Crafts: Bankura terracotta horses, Jamdani & Baluchari silk sarees, Dokra metal castings, Sholapith white cork art

points: Ancient kingdoms of Vanga, Pundra, and Gauda were major naval and trading centers
Pala Empire (8th–12th century) championed Mahayana Buddhism and established Somapura Mahavihara
Battle of Plassey in 1757 established British East India Company hegemony over Bengal
Kolkata served as imperial capital of British India until 1911; Bengal partitioned in 1947
source: Census of India 2011, Government of West Bengal, ODOP, Wikipedia

name: Andaman and Nicobar Islands
summary: Tropical island archipelago in the Bay of Bengal boasting pristine coral reefs, emerald lagoons, and historic Cellular Jail.
